subject: Recap + SDK/Auth/Routing options — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rob Ellis <rob.ellis@orionfin.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + SDK/Auth/Routing options — next steps

Hi Rob —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and the integration options we discussed so the tech team has a concise list to validate internally: 

Summary of requirements (from your call):
- Primary integration: product search & account enrichment powering customer support and decisioning flows.
- Security: AWS VPC, strict KMS requirements (HSM-backed), SOC 2 controls, and audit logs retention.
- Latency target: P95 < 350ms for the search path; some async enrichments can be >1s.
- Routing: US-only region for data residency.

Suggested integration patterns we recommend for Orion:

1) SDK setup & auth
- Preferred: Private deployment (Redwood Private) with customer VPC peering + customer-managed KMS (HSM) for key provisioning.
- Hosted option: short-lived OIDC tokens + per-environment API keys if you prefer managed control plane.
- We'll provide an SDK quickstart (Node/Python) with sample OIDC flow and token refresh built in.

2) Routing & fallback
- Primary route: model variants pinned to a latency-optimized LLM for core search.
- Fallback: lower-cost quantized model variant for bursts / capacity fallback; automatic signature mapping so prompts stay compatible.

3) Structured output & function/tool calling patterns
- Use explicit tool definitions for any outside-system calls (account_lookup, kyc_enrich, fraud_check).
- Prefer deterministic structured JSON outputs for downstream parsers (fields + confidence).
- For multi-step flows, we recommend a two-stage approach: synchronous token-generation for immediate responses, followed by an async fan-out for enrichment + embeddings generation where needed.

4) Embeddings & rerankers
- Compute document embeddings in a dedicated pipeline (batch or streaming) and store in your vector DB.
- Use a lightweight reranker on top of the ANN candidates before final scoring to meet latency SLO.

5) Tool/function calling & error handling (short version)
- Define clear tool contracts (input schema, timeout, retry semantics).
- Parallel vs serial: run enrichment tools in parallel when independent (e.g., fraud_check + external_enrichment) with a global deadline and best-effort aggregation.
- Fail-open vs fail-closed: default fail-open for non-critical enrichment (show partial results with a provenance flag), fail-closed for authorizations.
- Retries: idempotent retries + exponential backoff; include a circuit breaker on consistently failing external tools.

Ask / next steps
- Can you share the architecture diagram you mentioned and the SOC 2 evidence list? (attachments would be perfect)
- Proposed technical deep-dive: Tue 6/1 or Wed 6/2 — 60m with your infra & security leads + our platform engineer (Laura).
- I'll attach a short proposed tool-definition YAML and a checklist for the Private deployment prerequisites.

I'll hold off on a formal quote until we confirm Private vs Hosted routing needs.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + SDK/Auth/Routing options — next steps

Rob — perfect, thanks for the attachments. Answers inline and a short proposed plan.

1) Model updates / rollouts (Private):
- We handle pinned variants via your control plane. Rollouts are canary-based: we deploy to a small subset of capacity, run health checks and synthetic evals, and only promote when metrics meet your SLOs. We keep a history so you can roll back to a prior model snapshot instantly.

2) Token-level cost breakdowns:
- Yes — Redwood Console provides per-route + per-model token cost and latency breakdowns; we can add tags to requests to surface chargeback buckets.

Proposed technical plan (high level):
A) Tool definitions (attached YAML) — canonical examples below (we'll share a repo snippet in the drive):
- account_lookup:
  - description: return core account attributes from canonical source of truth
  - inputs: {account_id:string}
  - outputs: {name:string, tier:string, kyc_status:string}
  - timeout: 600ms
  - retry: 1 (idempotent)

- fraud_check:
  - description: external third-party fraud vendor call
  - inputs: {account_id:string, ip:string}
  - outputs: {score:float, flags:list}
  - timeout: 800ms
  - retry: 0 (no retries; use circuit breaker)

B) Parallel orchestration pattern (recommended)
- Step 1: synchronous LLM call for user-facing response (P95 <350ms)
- Step 2: kick an async fan-out to account_lookup, fraud_check, and external_enrich in parallel with a shared deadline (1.5s).
- Aggregation: merge best-effort results into the UI with a provenance flag and confidence.

C) Error handling approach
- Non-blocking enrichments = fail-open with "partial=true" in the response payload and a per-tool error field.
- Critical calls (authorization, KYC gating) = fail-closed with explicit error codes and an ALARM routed to your ops channel + Redwood fallback model where applicable.

D) SDK snippet (pseudo) — simple auth & call flow:
```
# Python pseudo
client = RedwoodClient(oidc_token=fetch_oidc())
resp = client.generate(model='r-infer-latency-optimized', prompt=payload, tools=["account_lookup"])
if resp.tools.account_lookup.status == 'ok':
  enrich = resp.tools.account_lookup.output
else:
  # handle partial
```

E) Next steps / meeting prep
- Confirm Tue 6/1 10:00am PT — Ben, Laura (eng lead) + Monica (solutions) will join.
- Ask Orion: share the final redacted arch diagram and a runnable subset of the SOC2 evidence mapping to owners.
- We'll prepare a one-pager on tool contracts and a short demo showing async fan-out + partial results.

Attaching: proposed-tool-definitions.yaml (stub) — I'll push the YAML to the shared drive and link in the meeting invite.

Ben
